subject.title: fix(eval): preserve OpenClaw and Hermes trajectories

question: Should native benchmark eligibility treat pre-agent infrastructure failures as neutral when the completed agent attempts have canonical model identity and real trajectories?
rationale: This is an audit and leaderboard-policy choice: the patch intentionally changes which partial native runs can become eligible, and that trust boundary cannot be resolved from implementation mechanics alone.

options.title: Approve the neutral-infrastructure policy
options.body: Accept the new behavior after reviewing a real native artifact pair that demonstrates the recovered trajectories and resulting eligibility report.

options.title: Require all expected tasks for eligibility
options.body: Keep infrastructure rows in the identity and trajectory requirements so any missing task remains ineligible until a rerun succeeds.

options.title: Separate partial-run eligibility
options.body: Add an explicit partial-run state or report field rather than treating excluded infrastructure failures as ordinary eligible coverage.

recommendation.title: Approve the neutral-infrastructure policy
recommendation.body: Accept the new behavior after reviewing a real native artifact pair that demonstrates the recovered trajectories and resulting eligibility report.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the active contributor for the native-evaluation stack and can provide the concrete run artifacts needed for the policy decision.
